resources.string: Disguise traffic · hide a message in a photo

Your 1:1 messages and attachments travel inside padded requests that look like ordinary web analytics, so their size and timing are harder to tell apart. If the disguised connection fails, messages wait — they are never sent undisguised.

Still visible: that you connect to oshi-messenger.com (server name and TLS fingerprint), and group messages, calls, push wake-ups and checks for new mail, which are not disguised. This is not anonymity and does not get around a block of the OSHI server — for that, use Disguise as photo.

Hide an end-to-end encrypted message for one contact inside an ordinary-looking photo, then send the photo through any app, e-mail or cloud drive — useful when OSHI itself is blocked. In a 1:1 chat: + → Disguise as photo.
You can also share a received photo to OSHI from any app.

Send it as a FILE or document. Apps that recompress photos (most social networks, WhatsApp, Signal or Telegram in photo mode, screenshots) erase the hidden message.
This hides the message from anyone looking at the photo. Forensic analysis can still detect that the photo carries hidden data, but cannot read it or tell who it is for.
No hidden message for you in this image. If it was sent as a photo, the app that carried it may have recompressed it — ask for it as a file.
